lines.en: It was 5:43 PM on a Friday and the fabric of reality was tearing again.
Deep beneath the surface, where there are more hidden truths than ones we’ve unearthed, three young creatures that called themselves “humans” decided to try and piece things back together.

Only one of them knew how to sew. One and a half on days where the medication didn’t make the second’s hands shake. But what they’d quickly find is that the fabric in question is not the kind you can easily mend.
And that no amount of textile work could make this place seem any more real to them than it already was.
Deeper and deeper they’d delve, counting grates that got worse at hiding the dark with light as the labyrinth pulled them further in.
The tunnels hadn’t learned to reshape themselves yet, but they were trying — like wounds that suture themselves with time and hide the important bits within us.
What were the tunnels trying to hide, though?
And why was only one of these alleged “humans” a bit concerned at the moment?
: Just a little further, guys. We should be getting there soon according to this map I made.
: I don’t know about this, Io...I’m starting to feel like we’re not allowed to be here.
: Yeah, ‘specially with all those signs sayin’ “Keep out” and stuff.
: It’s fine! We’ve been down here plenty of times and nobody’s caught us yet, right?
: Yeah...but I’ve never gone this deep before. My stomach’s starting to feel kind of weird. Like, isn’t it cold? I need a jacket. Let’s go get jackets and try again some other time.
: Maybe we shoulda just done that thing where one of us tries to toss somethin’ in from the top of the hole?
: That plan was Io’ed.
: The heck’s that mean?
: I think she means “trashed.”
: Bingo. The locations don’t match up. I went back to the sinkhole last weekend to try and get a better idea of how it lined up with where we are now and they’re just way too far apart.
: So unless this thing is like miles wide, I’m pretty sure we’re dealing with a different phenomenon entirely.
: I don’t really get it. But if you could teach me how to be this passionate about any sorta smart girl stuff, I’d really appreciate it.
: But if it’s not the sinkhole and it’s a different phenomenon, that makes it way scarier!
: Right?! Isn’t that fun?!
: No! What part of “scary” don’t you understand?!
: If you ask me, breaking into Sensei’s house was way scarier than this since we know for a fact that a monster lives there.
: Don’t talk about Ami like that! We’re probably going to kiss one day!
: Don’t! Ew!
: So, if there actually is some kinda monster, what’s the battle plan? Cause I ain’t rollin’ over for no demon now that I know what an orgasm feels like.
: I don’t know. I guess we probably just die.
: You’d be singin’ a different tune right now if you weren’t such a sexual.
: Miku, let’s leave Io to fight the monster on her own and...go wear jackets and talk about orgasms together!
: Sounds like my kinda Friday.
: Here! Straight ahead! We’re almost there!
: Come on! Just a little deeper!
: That sounds like my kinda Friday too.
: Miku, you’re gonna wind up hurting yourself again if you keep talking like that...
Further in the “humans” went, passing the last grate on the way to salvation.
But what they found upon arrival took on a form that none of them expected — especially the one who had already been here before.
: What the...
: Oh, good! Oh well! Looks like there’s nothing here. Time to turn around.
: Under construction? Construction of what?! No building needs a hole this deep!
: Ya think it might be some kinda earthquake thing? Or one of those thingies that hold a bunch of water in the event of floods or tidal waves somethin’?
: We live in Kumon-mi! We’re not going to get any tidal waves over here!
: Hey, the beach ain’t that far. I don’t know how big those things get.
: We’d know if they were constructing something of this size, though. And the fact that they haven’t done anything about the sinkhole yet makes me doubt it’s construction at all.
: Like, wouldn’t filling that thing in be the main priority here?
: Maybe...there was a second sinkhole? And we just didn’t know about it?
: But we’d see it from above ground and I didn’t find anything when I looked.
: Maybe you made a wrong turn or somethin’? Cause I ain’t great at followin’ directions either. Tried a new jogging route and got lost for like an hour the other day. Great exercise, though.
: What even is that? It looks more like a...screen than a sign. It’s gotta be, right? Like, who makes a sign that big?
: Maybe we should try and touch it to find out?
: Great idea. I nominate Miku.
: I could try. Looks like it ain’t attached to the ledge, though. So you guys might have to hold onto me and make sure I don’t fall.
: I take it back. Please don’t touch it.
: I agree. We don’t know if there are sensors on it or anything and touching it might alert someone to our presence.
: Now, I ain’t no hole expert, but I’m pretty sure if somebody’s got the technology to put this thing here, they’re probably already watchin’ us.
: Miku’s right. We should go back, Io. Everything about this seems kind of off. And you’ve said before that there was a door thing over here, right?
: Because all of this is starting to scream “evil government organization” to me. And it certainly doesn’t help that the new season of Stranger Things is still fresh in my mind.
: This isn’t some stupid TV show where the characters age ten years over the course of like one, though.
: Yeah. In fact, it kinda feels like we just ain’t agin’ at all sometimes.
: Ah! New Netflix show idea! Strangest Things! Think of all the money we could make! Those guys’ll license anything!
Confused and unamused, Io planned out her next move. Which direction could she take that might help her just to prove-
There was something more about this. Something sinister, corrupt. Who puts a sign inside a hole inside an empty aqueduct?
And if she were to jump, would it reach all the way down? “How deep does this thing go?” she thinks. “Would I even make a sound?”
There was a struggle. A big one. Internal and unheard. The kind that makes her want to emulate the acts of cuckoo birds.
She’d get nothing in return. Not an answer. Not a word. No replacement for the thing she’d lost, nor the type of nest she most prefers.
This compulsion. This fury. This stupid, lengthy, tragic journey- that ends in such a simple way it felt more like some duty’s jury.
This was all for nothing. Just like she was all for nothing. And the one thing she’d found in recent times that made her feel special was, in essence, also nothing.
What a letdown this became. So unfortunate. So lame. Guess it’s time to turn around and go back to retro PC games.
But then, suddenly, she noticed — from the corner of her eye — another body just beyond the bend. To which she’d question — why?
And so, suddenly, she’d vanish — and she’d leave her friends to die. To be swallowed by the “monster” as the bigger frog steals every fly.
They didn’t notice because they were dumb. They just stood and they stared as they twiddled their thumbs.
But I know something they don’t know. I know what’s above. I know what’s below. And I’ll show you, I swear, when I think it’s apropos.
For the moment, I’d like to preserve some neutrality. There’s a time and a place to breach confidentiality.
So enjoy the hospitality. Avoid some finality. And embrace or abhor all the forced sexuality. But keep this in mind-
Even the red string of fate can not repair this fabric.
But you know what can?
Immortality.
: You! Stop! You’re that girl, right?! The one that’s always showing up at our events?! What are you doing here?!
: Did you follow us?! Do you know what that...thing is?! Where are you going?!
: What, are you deaf too?! Come on! I know you were watching us! Don’t just walk away!
Io wanted to run, but she couldn’t. Something about the air here and how it blended with the darkness kept her movement stuck somewhere near 40%% its normal rate.
The thing with the air was the result of the same sort of invisible miasma exuded by the killers in classic slasher films that keep their victims from ever escaping.
The darkness was because it was dark.
Yet she scurried on like the “human” she was, trying to rapidly evolve in order to develop nightvision along the way and catch up with the child easier.
Unfortunately, evolution takes time when you are not at liberty to create something out of nothing.
: Hah...hah...hah...
Which few people are, need I remind you. It is hard to become a god. Almost as hard as running underwater, which I’m sure it often feels like you’re doing.
And no, that’s not from miasma. Nor is it some vengeful sea god (which there are many of). It’s just how water works or something.
I’m more accustomed to regular air, contrary to popular belief. Taking it. Giving it. Listening to how it sounds atop the roofs of building as I look out at the stars that decorate the skyline.
And when I see you all, you helpless, dysfunctional little ants, constantly exiting your death spiral to search for things that do not concern you, I can’t help but get mad.
I asked for a castle and this is what you give me? A mere tunnel?
That has always been my problem with ant farms. Once you reach the bottom, there’s nowhere left to go.
But wouldn’t it be great if you could see what was beneath you? Or taste the sky on your tongue? Or do all of those things you never can because you’re just built different?
The correct answer is “no.”
It wouldn’t.
Because greater things have greater fears.
And you should be happy with the ones you have down there in your farm.
For they are far less dangerous than what lurks below.
: Now...can we...finally...talk?...
: You’ve...backed...yourself...into a...corner!
: You have...nowhere else to...
: Now, I ain’t no hole expert, but I’m pretty sure if somebody’s got the technology to put this thing here, they’re probably already watchin’ us.
: Miku’s right. We should go back, Io. Everything about this seems kind of off. And you’ve said before that there was a door thing over here, right?
: Because all of this is starting to scream “evil government organization” to me. And it certainly doesn’t help that the new season of Stranger Things is still fresh in my- Io?
: Are you crying? What happened? Are you okay?
: It’s just a hole! It’s no big deal. There are...others. We can find other holes!
: You bring your pills? This another Yasu kinda thing? You ain’t gonna break if you don’t take ‘em right away, are ya?
: Uta’s right...we should go...
: Uhh...I mean...we can stay! I’m sorry if it seemed like I was scared. I’m not. Just...yeah! I’m not scared at all!
: Okay...
: But I am.
: Y...You are? But you’re never scared of anything. And just a second ago, you were-
: We shouldn’t be here...nobody should...
: Somethin’ ain’t right with Io. Think she might’a seen somethin’ we didn’t.
: Uhh...okay. Well, I guess we’ll leave then. You’re sure? You won’t be upset? You’re not just doing this for me?
: I need to leave...
: I don’t want her near me again.
: ...What?
: Just roll with it. I kinda wanna bail too.
: I-Io! Wait up! I don’t want to get lost in here!
It was 5:43 PM on a Friday.
No time had passed at all.
